findings.title: Reminders without a recipient or message never reach the retry limit
findings.body: When `sendTo` is empty or `message` is empty, this condition skips scheduling without incrementing `retryCount` or otherwise removing the reminder. The cron job will select the same unscheduled reminder on every run, so these unprocessable reminders are never cleaned up despite the retry limit.

findings.title: Concurrent failures can lose retry-count increments
findings.body: This writes an absolute value derived from the count read earlier, rather than incrementing the database value atomically. If overlapping cron invocations process the same reminder and both read the same `retryCount`, both can write the same next value; repeated overlaps can prevent the count from reaching 2, leaving failed reminders eligible for retries indefinitely. Use an atomic increment (and coordinate processing if concurrent sends must also be prevented).
